Dear Prof. Ogunlesi,

**RE: PROTOCOL DEVIATION REPORT – HY-2024-03 – SUBJECT 118**

I write to inform you of a minor protocol deviation that occurred on 12 August 2025, involving Subject 118 (screening number 118-014). The deviation was identified during routine source data verification conducted by the site clinical research associate on 14 August 2025.

**Details of the Deviation:**

Subject 118 attended the scheduled Week 12 study visit on 12 August 2025. Per protocol, vital signs were to be measured after the subject had rested for at least 10 minutes in a seated position. The study nurse, Mrs. Folake Adeyemi, recorded the blood pressure and heart rate after approximately 5 minutes of rest due to an oversight. The subject's vital signs were otherwise within normal limits and no clinical concerns were identified.

**Root Cause:**

The deviation was attributed to a high patient volume in the clinic on the day in question, which led to the study nurse inadvertently shortening the rest period. This was an isolated event and not indicative of a systemic issue.

**Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA):**

1. The study nurse has been re-trained on the protocol requirements for vital sign measurement, including the mandated rest period.
2. A laminated quick-reference card outlining the vital sign measurement procedure has been placed at the study visit workstation.
3. The site will conduct a refresher training session on protocol adherence for all study staff on 25 August 2025.

**Impact Assessment:**

The deviation is classified as minor. The subject's safety was not compromised, and the integrity of the study data is not affected. The deviation has been documented in the subject's source records and will be reported to the sponsor as per the protocol's reporting requirements.

I have also submitted a formal deviation report to the Health Research Ethics Committee (HREC) for their records, as required by our institutional policy.

Please let me know if you require any further information or wish to discuss the matter.

    from baseline in seated systolic blood pressure (SBP) at Week 12 to change from baseline in

    study and reduces participant burden.

    revised sample size calculation is provided in Appendix 3 of the amended protocol.

    that participants with secondary hypertension due to primary aldosteronism are excluded.

    prohibited concomitant medications, specifically excluding the use of other
    angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs)
    during the trial.

We respectfully request that this amendment be reviewed and approved in accordance with the
NAFDAC Clinical Trial Regulation 2021. We are available to provide any further information
required.

Dear Prof. Ogunlesi,

**RE: PROTOCOL DEVIATION REPORT – HY-2024-03 – SUBJECT 118**

I write to inform you of a minor protocol deviation that occurred on 12 August 2025, involving Subject 118 (screening number 118-014). The deviation was identified during routine source data verification conducted by the site clinical research associate on 14 August 2025.

**Details of the Deviation:**

Subject 118 attended the scheduled Week 12 study visit on 12 August 2025. Per protocol, vital signs were to be measured after the subject had rested for at least 10 minutes in a seated position. The study nurse, Mrs. Folake Adeyemi, recorded the blood pressure and heart rate after approximately 5 minutes of rest due to an oversight. The subject's vital signs were otherwise within normal limits and no clinical concerns were identified.

**Root Cause:**

The deviation was attributed to a high patient volume in the clinic on the day in question, which led to the study nurse inadvertently shortening the rest period. This was an isolated event and not indicative of a systemic issue.

**Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA):**

1. The study nurse has been re-trained on the protocol requirements for vital sign measurement, including the mandated rest period.
2. A laminated quick-reference card outlining the vital sign measurement procedure has been placed at the study visit workstation.
3. The site will conduct a refresher training session on protocol adherence for all study staff on 25 August 2025.

**Impact Assessment:**

The deviation is classified as minor. The subject's safety was not compromised, and the integrity of the study data is not affected. The deviation has been documented in the subject's source records and will be reported to the sponsor as per the protocol's reporting requirements.

I have also submitted a formal deviation report to the Health Research Ethics Committee (HREC) for their records, as required by our institutional policy.

Please let me know if you require any further information or wish to discuss the matter.

Regards,

**Dr. Ngozi Okafor**
Regulatory Affairs Officer

Subject 087, a 54-year-old female, was admitted to LUTH on 27 August 2025 with a diagnosis of acute pyelonephritis. The subject's medical history includes recurrent urinary tract infections, which is a known risk factor for this condition.

The subject responded well to intravenous antibiotics and was discharged in stable condition on 31 August 2025. She has been advised to complete a course of oral antibiotics and to attend a follow-up visit at the study site on 12 September 2025.

**Reporting:**

The SAE has been reported to the sponsor within the required 24-hour timeframe. A detailed SAE report has also been submitted to the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) and the Health Research Ethics Committee (HREC) in accordance with regulatory requirements.
